name: American Revolutionary War
causes: Taxation without representation (Stamp Act, Townshend Acts, Tea Act)
Enforcement of the Coercive / Intolerable Acts
Suppression of self-governance and quartering of British troops
Enlightenment ideals of liberty and John Locke's social contract theory
consequences: Treaty of Paris (1783) officially recognizing U.S. independence
Establishment of the first modern constitutional democratic republic
Drafting of the United States Constitution and Bill of Rights (1787–1791)
Global wave of democratic and anti-colonial revolutions (including France and Latin America)
description: An ideological and political revolution that occurred in colonial North America, resulting in the thirteen British colonies establishing the independent United States of America.

name: The French Revolution
causes: Severe financial crisis and royal debt following Seven Years' War and American aid
Inequitable Estate System (exemption of clergy and nobility from direct taxation)
Widespread food shortages, harvest failures, and soaring bread prices
Dissemination of Enlightenment philosophy (Rousseau, Voltaire, Montesquieu)
consequences: Abolition of the feudal order and absolute Bourbon monarchy
Promulgation of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
The Reign of Terror and political restructuring under the Jacobins
Rise of Napoleon Bonaparte and transformation of European legal codes (Napoleonic Code)
description: A period of radical political and societal upheaval in France that fundamentally transformed modern political history, dismantling the Ancien Régime.

name: World War I (The Great War)
causes: Militarism: Arms race, naval competition between Britain and Germany
Alliances: Interlocking secret defensive pacts (Triple Entente vs. Triple Alliance)
Imperialism: Clashing colonial interests in Africa and Asia
Nationalism: Slavic self-determination in the Balkans ('Powder Keg of Europe')
Immediate Catalyst: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (June 28, 1914)
consequences: Collapse of four great imperial dynasties: German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian, and Ottoman empires
Treaty of Versailles (1919) imposing heavy reparations and territorial losses on Germany
Bolshevik Revolution and emergence of the Soviet Union (1917)
Creation of the League of Nations to arbitrate international disputes
Redrawing of boundaries in Central Europe and the Middle East (Sykes-Picot Agreement)
description: One of the deadliest global conflicts in history, fought across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, introducing industrialized trench warfare, poison gas, tanks, and aerial combat.

name: World War II
causes: Resentment over harsh terms of the 1919 Treaty of Versailles
Rise of totalitarian fascist regimes in Germany (Hitler) and Italy (Mussolini)
Aggressive territorial expansionism: Germany in Europe, Imperial Japan in Manchuria/China
Failure and appeasement policies of the League of Nations
Immediate Trigger: German invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939
consequences: Complete defeat and unconditional surrender of the Axis powers; division of Germany
The Holocaust uncovered: Genocide of six million European Jews and millions of others
Invention and first wartime use of nuclear weapons (Hiroshima and Nagasaki)
Founding of the United Nations (1945) with permanent Security Council
Dawn of the Cold War bipolar rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union
Acceleration of worldwide decolonization in Asia and Africa
description: The deadliest conflict in human history, involving tens of millions of combatants and civilians across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Pacific, fundamentally reshaping modern global geopolitical institutions.

name: The Fall of Constantinople
causes: Long-term territorial decline and isolation of the Byzantine Empire
Aggressive military expansion of the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mehmed II
Strategic geographic location controlling Black Sea trade routes between Europe and Asia
consequences: End of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire after over 1,000 years
Constantinople transformed into the capital of the Ottoman Empire (Istanbul)
Exodus of Byzantine scholars to Italy, heavily accelerating the Renaissance
Disruption of European overland trade routes to Asia, driving the Age of Discovery and maritime exploration
description: The capture of the capital of the Byzantine Empire by the invading Ottoman army under Sultan Mehmed II, widely considered by historians as marking the end of the Middle Ages.
